newsitem.title: USA: Clinton puts school improvement in campaign spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Clinton puts school improvement in campaign spotlight.

text.p: Taking advantage of every opening to spur his re-election campaign, President (Bill) Clinton on Thursday was set to use a report critical of teacher training and performance as a springboard for promising to improve education.

Aides said Clinton would order Education Secretary Richard Reilly to tell states how they can use existing federal funds to respond to the findings of a bipartisan commission headed by North Carolina Gov. Jim Hunt, which concluded that many teachers need to be better trained and required to meet higher standards.
The president also planned to direct the Education Department to establish an information clearing-house and issue annual "report cards" on teacher training and performancem, they said.

By promising action on the Hunt report, Clinton clearly hoped to neutralise Republican challenger Bob Dole's convention claim that powerful teacher unions -- a key Democratic Party constituent group -- are to blame for problems in America's classrooms.
But presidential adviser Bruce Reed said Clinton "has been working on these issues for 15 years."

During a visit to the Morris Dailey Elementary School, Clinton also planned to announce the award of $1.3 million in "school charter" money for California, aides said. Washington gave the state $700,000 last year to enable teachers, principals and parents to establish their own schools by obtaining a public charter.
"It's a way to promote greater choice within the public school system," an official said.

Clinton, on his 27th visit to California since he entered the White House in 1993, later was to attend fundraisers in Silicon Valley and Los Angeles that were expected to raise about $4.5 million for Democratic party campaign coffers.
Superstar entertainer Barbra Streisand, a longtime Clinton supporter and close friend of the president, was to headline the Los Angeles gala.
California offers 54 of the 270 electoral votes needed to win the Nov. 5 election, and Clinton led Dole in the state by 23 percentage points in the latest independent statewide survey.
More surprising was Clinton's showing in neighbouring Arizona, a state that went to the Republicans in the last 11 presidential elections.
Clinton campaigned in Arizona on Wednesday, and campaign officials said the latest opinion polls showed him leading Dole there by eight percentage points.
The last Democrat to carry Arizona was President Harry Truman in 1948.
"For the moment we have a lead. It is an extraordinary place for a Democratic candidate to have a lead," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
